title: Playing with Fess; cane-farm dance; Barnes and Lee
summary: He alternated cornet and violin in Fess's first band and recalls a dance on a country cane farm.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Fiddlers and reading violinists of New Orleans

blocks.x: You must have had your carnet when you played with Fess, didn't you, in that first band that Fess was in? Yes.
Because he said he played, sometime he'd play carnet and then...
And then when you'd get the heart, his lip would give out.

Then I played violin, yeah. Great. Oh, Jesus, that's been, uh, oof. That's the first time I've carried him down in the country on a cane farm. You know, in the cane cart in the morning. When a big cart, he told me about that once. Yeah, had three mules in that.
What do you call it, the cane cart?

Yeah, the whole cane in it. Yeah, yeah. And they come to get us, uh, the carnet down there, we finished grinding, you know. Just giving a little dance down there for the people. And the Fess, and, uh, I believe I carried a, uh, uh, uh, um, that fella insurance man, there, his cousin.
Oh, uh, Humphrey, uh... Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah.
Jules Lee was the, wait, Jules Barnes.
The trombone, and Lee was the drummer.
